description_full: Park National Corporation operates as the bank holding company for Park National Bank that provides commercial banking and trust services in the United States. The company offers deposits, such as demand, savings, and time accounts; trust and wealth management services; cash management services; safe deposit operations; electronic funds transfers; Internet and mobile banking solutions with bill pay service; credit cards; and various additional banking-related services. It also provides commercial loans, including financing for industrial and commercial properties, financing for equipment, inventory and accounts receivable, acquisition financing, and commercial leasing, as well as for consumer finance companies; commercial real estate loans comprising mortgage loans to developers and owners of commercial real estate; originates financing leases primarily for the purchase of commercial vehicles, operating/manufacturing equipment, and municipal vehicles/equipment; consumer loans, such as automobile, recreational vehicle, and watercraft loans; consumer finance services; home equity lines of credit; and residential real estate and construction loans, as well as instalment loans and commercial loans. In addition, the company offers aircraft financing services; and ParkDirect, a personal banking application. Park National Corporation was founded in 1908 and is headquartered in Newark, Ohio.

financial_summary: Park National Corporation is a mid-cap financial services business with a $3.1B market cap on $664M of annual revenue.
The top line has compounded at +11% over the past three years and +8% annually across the full decade, a respectable pace for a business of this size.
Returns on capital run at 11% against a 8% cost of capital, a 3-point spread that creates value, though narrow enough that competitive pressure could close it.

The business throws off $192M in free cash flow — roughly 29 cents on every revenue dollar, which is the owner-earnings figure that actually belongs to shareholders, and cash conversion sits at 1.10× so those profits are backed by real cash.

On the balance sheet, the balance sheet carries net cash, which is the gold standard: the business never has to make desperate decisions in a bad year, and thin 2.0× interest coverage leaves no room for a bad year.
Shareholder yield of 3.2% reflects a genuine commitment to returning capital rather than empire-building, and insiders hold 2.2% of the shares.

Interest rate regime shifts — a rapid move in rates can invert the yield curve, crush bond portfolios, and trigger deposit flight simultaneously.
